observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a white bowl or plate holding a yellow liquid arranged in an open U-shaped ring, with a paler, foamy/solidified yellow mass filling the upper arc of the ring. For the first ~0.7 s the scene is static with no tool present. From t≈0.8 s a metal knife blade (serrated edge visible) enters from the lower right and its tip is pressed into the yellow mass, then swept back and forth across the pool.
visible_changes: Frames 1-12 show no object motion: the yellow pool and bowl are at rest.
At frame 13 a knife blade appears at the right side of the yellow ring, tip embedded in the substance.
From frames 14-41 the knife tip is repositioned repeatedly—right side, center, left side—moving across the yellow mass in a back-and-forth spreading/stirring motion.
The foamy yellow mass and the surrounding liquid are locally displaced and deformed as the blade passes through them; the overall ring shape persists.
The knife's orientation and insertion point change frame to frame, indicating continuous manual motion rather than a single static pose.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the yellow substance (melted butter, oil, etc.) and of the tool's operator are not shown.
What precedes the knife's appearance and what follows after the last frame are outside the excerpt.
Whether the spreading continues or stops after t=2.67 s is unknown.
uncertain_details: Minor shifts of the bowl edge and highlights between frames may be handheld camera jitter rather than object motion; camera movement is not clearly separable from the scene.
The exact mechanical effect of the blade (mixing vs. scraping) cannot be confirmed from the top-down view.
